subject: Cloud Computing
title: What Is FinOps?
description: A 60-second lesson on What Is FinOps?.

hook.text: Engineering builds fast and finance pays the bill. Nobody talks to each other. FinOps bridges that gap.

buildup.text: FinOps — Financial Operations — is a practice where engineering, finance, and business collaborate on cloud spending.

discovery.text: The FinOps Foundation defines three phases: inform (understand costs), optimize (reduce waste), and operate (govern).

twist.text: FinOps isn't about cutting costs. It's about spending intentionally — sometimes that means spending more.

climax.text: Companies with mature FinOps practices save 20-30% on cloud. The discipline pays for itself many times over.

punchline.text: FinOps makes cloud costs everyone's job. Not just finance.

quiz.question: What is the primary goal of FinOps?
options: Collaborative, intentional management of cloud spending across teams
Eliminating all cloud costs by moving everything on-premises
Automating invoice processing for cloud services

details.summary: FinOps is a practice that brings financial accountability to cloud spending by combining engineering, finance, and business teams. It uses real-time cost data, shared ownership, and continuous optimization to maximize the business value of every cloud dollar spent.
details.whyItMatters: Cloud spending is distributed across teams and hard to control centrally. FinOps creates the culture, processes, and tools needed to manage cloud costs as a shared responsibility.
takeaways: Combines engineering, finance, and business for cost accountability
Uses real-time data to drive continuous cost optimization
Shared ownership replaces central IT budget gatekeeping

faq.question: What are the phases of FinOps?
faq.answer: Inform: give teams visibility into their spending with dashboards and allocation. Optimize: identify and implement savings opportunities like reservations and right-sizing. Operate: continuously monitor, set budgets, and automate cost governance across the organization.

faq.question: Who is responsible for FinOps?
faq.answer: A dedicated FinOps team or practitioner coordinates the practice, but responsibility is shared. Engineers make cost-aware architecture decisions, finance teams forecast and budget, and leadership sets spending targets. Cloud cost is everyone's responsibility.
